newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn crop 30 pct planted, soy 10 pct sown.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn crop 30 pct planted, soy 10 pct sown.

text.p: Thirty percent of Indiana's intended corn acreage was planted as of Sunday, well ahead of normal, the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.
Last year, seven percent of the area was planted on the comparable day, and the five-year average is eight percent.

The best progress was made in the central region of the state where 40 percent of the area had been planted. In the north, 33 percent had been planted with only four percent planted in the south. Record progress was achieved in 1988 when 43 percent was planted by April 30.
Soybean plantings were ten percent complete, well ahead of the five-year average of one percent. Last year plantings had not begun.
"Dry weather allowed planting and tillage operations to advance rapidly this past week," the report said.

The winter wheat crop was rated 63 percent good to excellent, up from 57 percent a week earlier and only 20 percent good to excellent at this time last year. Fifty two percent was jointed versus a five-year average of 38 percent.
Topsoil moisture was 15 percent surplus, 75 percent adequate, nine percent short and one percent very short.
